sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A compact desert agave with fleshy blue-grey leaves edged with teeth and tipped by a spine. Horticultural profiles give a rosette about 0.5–1 m tall and 1–1.5 m across; its flowering stalk can reach about 2 m. Yellow flowers grow in clusters.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: Ethnobotanical sources report traditional food use of flowers and other parts of desert agaves, including A. deserti. The cited uses involve preparation such as cooking or roasting; they do not establish that raw plant parts are safe to eat.

sources.title: Food Plants of the Sonoran Desert — University of Arizona Press
